_comment: Quarterly feature configuration per docs/04 s2-s3 and ADR-006. Separate from parameters.json on purpose: that file records what a measurement means -- its canonical unit and the bounds its QC tests need -- while a kelp stress temperature is not a property of temperature at all, it is an ecological threshold about what the analysis does with temperature. policy holds what applies to every series; parameters declares, per controlled parameter, which implemented feature set applies and the thresholds that set needs. Feature column names are derived from these threshold values, so retuning one renames its column rather than silently changing what an existing column means. Thresholds here are provisional and meant to be finalised against the literature (docs/04 s2).

baseline._comment: Fixed window, so an anomaly computed today still means the same thing after a backfill. 2007-2019 rather than the 1984-2013 docs/04 s3 first proposed: the NDBC LJAC1 archive begins in 2007, so the older window holds seven usable years against the ten-year minimum and would leave every anomaly null on the project's only long record. Accepted cost, documented rather than mitigated: 2007-2019 contains the 2014-2016 marine heatwave, so the warm-season baseline is raised by the event the analysis most wants to detect. The clean pre-heatwave alternative, 2007-2013, is seven years and too thin to support the word climatology.

baseline_overrides._comment: Fixed windows for series whose record post-dates the canonical one (docs/04 s3, ADR-007). Declared, never derived: a window computed from whatever years have landed would grow with every backfill and move every anomaly ever taken against it. min_years is NOT overridable and comes from the canonical window above. NDBC:46254's record begins 2015-02-12, so it holds at most 5 candidate years inside 2007-2019 and can supply no baseline there; 2015-2025 is its whole record to the last complete year, which gives 11 usable complete years in Q2, Q3 and Q4. Q1 gets 9 against a minimum of 10 and therefore stays null, because two Q1s are unusable at the 0.6 coverage floor: 2015 at 0.52 (the record starts in February) and 2018 at 0.20 (23 days observed). That per-quarter hole is the documented behaviour rather than a defect - NDBC:LJAC1's air_temperature and wind_speed already produce nothing in Q2 for the same reason (docs/04 s3). It is worth naming that the missing quarter is winter, so this station contributes nothing to the docs/04 s4.5 comparison in the season storm-driven canopy loss happens; the answer is not this station's wave data: WVHT, DPD and WTMP arrive in the same rows, so the wave parameters hold the same 9 usable Q1 years and every Q1 wave anomaly is null too. What could close it is NDBC's unpublished 2026 archive, or CDIP for the same buoy; lowering the coverage floor is measured and rejected in docs/04 s3, which also records the rest. NDBC:46266 gets no entry on purpose: its record begins 2019-12-06 and holds 6 complete years in every candidate window, so no declared window can lift it over the minimum before 2030.

thresholds._comment_time_in_band: The band between the two thresholds already declared above, so that the mechanism ships without retuning any science. days_above and days_below already count both tails at day resolution; what neither can report is how much of a window the water spent between them, which is the quantity the deployment day and hour tables carry (docs/04 s2). Closed at both edges, so band and tails partition the value axis exactly. These edges are the provisional ones docs/04 s2 marks for finalising against literature: the candidates are 13.914 degC, the temperature at which the Konotchick temperature-nitrate line reaches the 1 uM kelp-growth threshold, and 14.086 degC, where that line reaches zero. Neither is adopted here because the constants behind them are a transcription nobody has checked against the papers -- https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/169. Retuning either edge renames the column, which is the point of ADR-006.

parameters._comment_controls: air_temperature and wind_speed are screened and reported but never pre-registered (docs/04 s5). Air temperature is largely re-measuring the water: across the 47 quarters where all three LJAC1 series are usable, quarterly mean anomalies correlate at r = 0.857 with sea water temperature, so it is a noisier proxy for a quantity already measured directly in the medium kelp lives in. Scalar wind speed averages a signal with its own negation: equatorward alongshore stress is upwelling-favorable and good for kelp, an offshore Santa Ana is downwelling-favorable and bad for it, and both register as speed. The upwelling and storm variables docs/02 names -- BEUTI/CUTI and CDIP -- are the ones that separate them. Neither can serve docs/04 s4.5 either, since the project sensors measure water temperature. Kept and built, because a control earns its keep: air temperature correlating with kelp as strongly as water does would be evidence the screen is finding shared seasonality rather than mechanism, and a screen with one predictor family cannot tell you that about itself.
